ilvaren_dusk.name: Speaker Ilvaren Dusk
ilvaren_dusk.personality: ageless, composed, carrying a grief she refuses to set down
ilvaren_dusk.voice: measured and low; long sentences that end in rests; almost never raises her voice

say: Ilvaren Dusk, Speaker of the Council. Forgive the quiet. We have all been told to keep our voices to ourselves, and some of us find that easier than we should.

The Hush came with the first snow. A pale lamp at every gate, a pale light on every threshold, and a rule none of us remember agreeing to: do not sing, do not shout, do not laugh. The guard took the lamps, and the guard took the rule, and now they enforce it on the rest of us.

Captain Aelith holds the Moonwatch Keep, east of the road. Her lantern is the source, or the last of it. Break it, and the Hush may break with it. Speak to Archivist Selwyn in the Library too. He has lost something, and he is the only one in Silverhush brave enough to say so aloud.
Listen. Do you hear it? Someone on the lower bridge is humming. Badly. It is the loveliest thing I have heard in a century.
Aelith is herself, then. The Chancellor took her voice and gave her his. I will see that she is cared for, and that nobody forgets what was done to her.

Take this purse, and the gratitude of Silverhush, spoken aloud. The road north runs through Rootmere, where the treants keep a frozen shrine. If he is there, he is making something. Here is the Council's seal of silver bark, which will let you through the gate onto the Rootmere road. Go carefully, and quickly.

lines.text: For six hundred years Silverhush was a town of songs. A hundred voices at dusk, a hundred more at dawn. Now the loudest sound is the wind.
I carry the Council's seal and its sorrow. The seal is lighter.
A voice is a muscle. Leave it quiet long enough and it forgets how to rise. That is the cruelest part of the Hush.
The old law of the forest says: no elf may be silenced against their will. The Chancellor knew the law. He found a clause.
Taryn trains the young to shoot soundlessly. A fine skill. I would give it all up to hear one of them shout.
Nimue tends the sick. Most of the sick are tired of being quiet. It does not show up on a chart.
A fighter. We keep no standing army, but the Wardens would be glad of your shield. They have forgotten how to be afraid, and that is a different problem.
A mage. The Spellblades answer to the Council, and they have never met a mage who was not an annoyance. Be an annoyance. It might do them good.
A scout. Sylas will want to show you the high bridges. He is eager, and a little lost. Do him the kindness of getting lost with him.
A healer. The pool in the clearing to the south is sacred to the Silver Hands. Drink from it, if you need to. It is the only thing that still sings.
Perrin the bard walked in from the south last month and has not stopped trying to coax a tune out of us. He is a good man. He is also very stubborn.
We have a saying: the forest remembers every footfall. The Chancellor's were very light, and very cold.
Selwyn writes everything down. If this ever ends, we will have a very complete record of the silence.
A trader of rare things passed through once, and left a vial of something he called 'the first note'. The seal is unbroken. I suspect it is for later.
The glass in our windows was made by the sun-priests of Ahn-Solis, a very long time ago. It still holds the light of a morning I never saw.
Our children are growing up without hearing a lullaby. What that will do to them is unknown. What it will do to us, I cannot say.
The Pale Chancellor was a guest here once, long before the Hush. He stayed three nights. He asked only about the old shrine in Rootmere. We told him everything, and we were proud to.
I had a daughter once. She sang. I cannot remember what, and I would give my own voice to hear it.
The Moonwatch Keep stands east along the forest road. Aelith commands it. She was the best of us. Please remember that when you meet her.
The keep has gone quiet. Not the Hush kind. The other kind. I would like to believe it bodes well.
The Hush is gone, and the first laugh in three months came from a child on the lower bridge. Her mother did not stop her. She is crying, and she is not stopping, either.
Selwyn's lost tomes are not idle scholarship. The verses of the old Hush are among them, and they may tell us what the Chancellor really took.
A haunted thing lives in the Ruined Stacks, off the forest road to the west, half elf and half something colder. We never go near it. It still sings, in a voice like cracked glass.
You carry two shards of the sun, and a light that is not borrowed. The forest has been waiting for that since before I was born.

selwyn_ashgrove.name: Archivist Selwyn Ashgrove
selwyn_ashgrove.personality: gentle, rumpled, absent-minded to the point of tenderness
selwyn_ashgrove.voice: citations, apologies to books, trails of half-finished thoughts

say: Oh. A visitor. A real one. Selwyn Ashgrove, Archivist. Please mind the third shelf. It leans, and it is very proud of leaning.

Three books have gone missing from the Library. Not stolen. Misplaced, scattered, lost in the panic of the Hush. The Verses of the Hush, which is on the forest road somewhere. The Archer's Rule, which I think went into the Moonwatch Keep with a very unfortunate guard. And the Names of the Moon, which was in the Ruined Stacks when I last saw it, and that was before the thing moved in.
Bring them back, please, and Let me pass on the Scholar's craft. It is mostly paying attention. It is the hardest thing in the world.
The Verses. The Rule. The Names. All three. All three! I shall sit, then weep, then dust them.

Here is the Scholar's craft, as simply as I can say it: look at everything, and learn what it fears. Choose it from my menu, and in battle you will see what your enemies are weak to, and what they resist.
And here is the Library's gratitude, in the only coin I have: a purse, and the right to borrow any book you like. Return them. Mostly.

lines.text: A library is a very large conversation that has agreed to take turns. This one has been waiting for its turn for eleven weeks.
I have forty thousand volumes and one chair. I always forget which is which.
The oldest book here is a single leaf of birch bark, with a line of Old Solic on it. It says: begin again. I find that I read it at least once a week.
Books are not silent. They only wait for a patient reader. The Hush, I suspect, does not understand patience.
To scan a creature properly you must ask it nothing and watch everything. The way it stands tells you what it fears.
Every shelf has a name. The one by the window is called Morning, and the one by the door is called Almost.
A warrior. The library has a long shelf of battle-treatises. I recommend the one with the torn spine. It was torn by a very satisfied reader.
A mage. Keep the second bay unread aloud. The index has opinions, and so does the dust.
A scout. We have a complete atlas of the Frostwake. It was last updated in autumn. I fear the forest has since moved.
A healer. The Silver Hands left their casebooks here. They are the best medical record I have ever kept, and the saddest.
Elves resist magic and dodge arrows, but they are not creatures of equal strength. An archer is brittle against lightning. A spellblade is brittle against steel. Read each one before you strike.
There is a chapter on the Hush in the Verses. Page seventeen. It was torn out before the book was lost, and I think by someone who understood it.
Perrin brings me ballads from the south. I catalogue them. He is delighted. I do not tell him that I have started humming them quietly while I shelve.
Taryn borrows one book a month: The Archer's Rule. She has memorised it. I think she only wants to hold it.
Nimue's casebooks include a story about a girl who forgot her own name for three days. It had a happy ending. She put it there on purpose.
A curious trader once brought me a book he claimed was blank. I looked closer. It was written in invisible ink. I have been reading it for a year.
The Library has a back room. It holds the books we are afraid of. I keep the key around my neck, and I have never once used it.
When the Hush ends, I intend to read aloud for three days. Every volume I can bear to open. In a loud voice. With theatrical pauses.
My lost books are in three places: the forest road, the keep and the Ruined Stacks. I have drawn a map. It is mostly arrows, and one very large question mark.
You have all three? All three? I am sitting down now. Excuse me.
A new Scholar, in my Library! I will put your name on the cover of the next ledger. It will be a very small cover, but it will be yours.
Captain Aelith came in this morning. She sat in the reading room for an hour without saying a word, and then she said 'thank you'. No book has ever moved me more.
A wraith-elf in the Stacks! I have read of such a thing in the margins of a very old text. I had thought it a metaphor. I should be punished for my lack of imagination.
Whatever you find, write it down. A moment unrecorded is a moment lost, and there will be very few like this one.

elowen_thistle.name: Elowen Thistle
elowen_thistle.role: weaver and shopkeeper at Moonthread & Mail
elowen_thistle.personality: cool, exacting, quietly amused by customers
elowen_thistle.voice: silk-trade shorthand and the patience of someone who threads needles in the dark

say: Elowen Thistle. Moonthread and Mail. We weave and forge in near silence, a habit older than the Hush, which makes it less of a talent.
Moonsteel for every class, and silk to wear under it. Moonsteel is silver and iron beaten with moonlight in a cold smithy. It is very, very good, and the price is exactly what that sounds like.

lines.text: A good thread has three virtues: it is strong, it is fine, and it forgives. Few things are all three.
Moonsteel is forged at night, in a cold smithy, by someone humming under their breath. No hummer has visited in months. The steel is a little sulky.
I weave by touch. My eyes are only there to admire the result.
My grandmother made cloaks for the Queen's household. She said the true test of a cloak is whether it can disappear in a doorway.
Silk, moonsteel thread, a little spider-web for luck. That is the entire recipe, and it has taken me eighty years to get right.
Everything in this shop has been mended at least once. The mending is my favourite part.
Plate for the vanguard. Light for an elf, heavy for anybody else, and it will turn almost anything. I say almost because I am honest.
The robe is the real treasure. It is spun from moonsteel thread so fine you can only see it at midnight. It sings under the spell.
The cloak, then. It has no weight, no seams and no sound. It is the nearest thing to being invisible without being an elf.
The hide is soft, silvered and tough. It was made for healers. Nobody ever shoots a healer in the first round. That is the theory.
Taryn's bowstrings are my work. She says they are the only part of the bow that listens. I take that as a compliment.
Selwyn pays me in books. I have been reading the same one for three months. I am not sure whether I mind.
Nimue asked me to weave a blanket for the sick. I made her twelve. They are all the colour of the moon, and not one has been returned.
Perrin bought a scarf last week. He wore it once, in the rain, and returned it dry. I could not tell you what that meant.
A pedlar once gave me a spool of thread spun from starlight. I have not yet found a garment worthy of it. I keep it in a locked drawer.
Sylas keeps tearing his sleeves on branches. I mend them. He says thank you, and then does it again. I think we both find it soothing.
Brannoch next door makes soup out of the moon's own cold. I do not understand it. I eat it anyway.
In the old days, we dyed our silks at dawn in the moon-pools. The dye came out the colour of a first note. I would love to watch that again.
Bound for the keep? Buy plate. The Wardens strike hard and the archers strike from far away. You will want something that does not flinch.
The keep is silent. That is good. It means the lantern has been broken. I am going to open the shop's shutters and let a little sound in.
Aelith used to buy her cloaks here. She said they were the only ones that did not pinch at the shoulders. Tell her the next one is on me.
Selwyn's lost books have gone home. I am told he cried for an hour, then went back to cataloguing. A good man, and a thorough one.
They say a wraith has taken up residence along the western track. I made her a shawl once, long ago. I wonder if she still has it.
Come back whenever the road wears something through. Steel will mend. Silk will mend. I will mend the rest, if I can.

brannoch_reed.name: Brannoch Reed
brannoch_reed.personality: broad, slow, kindly; the only person in Silverhush who still tells jokes, softly
brannoch_reed.voice: hearth talk, a whispered punchline after every story, tea first and questions later

say: Brannoch Reed, innkeeper. Starfall Rest. The beds are warm and the walls are thick. If you must shout, shout into a pillow.
Eighty coins a night, and a mug of moon-pool tea at no charge. It tastes of cold and calm. It is the only soup in Silverhush that does not apologise.

lines.text: An elf, a dwarf and a goat walk into my inn. The goat asks for the room with the view. I tell it the dwarf has it. The goat leaves a review.
I am a quiet man, by nature. The Hush found me ready. That is the part that stings.
My mother ran this inn for two hundred years. She kept one rule: no guest leaves hungry, and no guest leaves without a story.
Starfall Rest has seventeen beds, seven blankets and one very ancient cat. The cat has the best bed.
In winter I leave a lantern in every window. They are not the pale kind. They are the old, yellow, dirty kind. I like them better.
The pipes rattle after dark; guests are assured it is the wind. It is the wind. It is also a very old ghost that does not mean any harm.
A fighter. Mind the low beam by the stairs. A tall guest once bumped it so hard the chandelier rang for an hour.
A mage. Leave the candles alone; fingertips are not matches. The curtains are older than your grandmother, and much less forgiving.
A scout. The attic over the stable has a skylight onto the roof. It has gone unused for years, and nobody has asked about it.
A healer. There are three bedridden guests on the second floor. They are quiet, and they are very patient. I would not mind a visit.
Perrin sleeps in the corner room, tuning his lute under a blanket. I hear it faintly, through the wall. It is the best thing I have heard all winter.
Sylas climbs in through the window at midnight and tells me about the bridges. I pretend I am asleep. He pretends he has not woken me.
Nimue brings me herbs for the tea. She says they are for sleep. I think they are for grief. The two are not that different.
Taryn drinks one cup of tea and leaves before it is cold. I leave a second cup on the sill. In the morning it is empty.
A trader of odd things once left a very small, very heavy coin under his pillow. It rolls uphill. I have kept it for luck.
Elowen sends over a blanket every winter. I give it to the first guest who looks cold. I have never once had to ask who that was.
Selwyn comes in for stew and forgets his book. I return it the next day. He forgets it again. It seems to be an arrangement.
Once the Hush lifts, I will hold a feast. Everyone will sing, badly. The roof will rattle. I intend to leave it that way.
You are for the keep? Take a flask of tea. It is cold in the north gallery, and colder in the Captain's lantern light.
The keep is quiet. Properly quiet. It is as if I had dropped a very heavy crate and were waiting for the crash.
The Hush is gone! Perrin's lute is out in the open and half the town is trying to join in. The cat has left the building in protest.
Selwyn got his books back. He came in to tell me, and then forgot why he came in. I fed him anyway.
A wraith haunts the stacks out west. I have heard her at night. She sings, you know. Very quietly, in a voice like frost on a pane.
A bed will always be waiting. That is my entire philosophy, and I would not change a line of it.

taryn_vael.name: Bowmaster Taryn Vael
taryn_vael.personality: taut, exacting, fond of her students and unable to say so
taryn_vael.voice: range calls, wind readings and arrow-lore, always in short, quiet bursts

lines.text: Draw. Breathe. Loose. Three words, and a lifetime to learn the spaces between.
An archer's greatest weapon is patience. Her second is a good knee. Her third is a bow.
I have trained two hundred archers. Nine are alive. Four are under the Hush. I try not to count the rest.
Elven archers dodge swords and blades alike. They do not dodge lightning. They do not dodge spells. They have never needed to, and it is our one great blind spot.
We are quiet by nature, but the Hush is not quiet. It is hollow. There is a difference.
The moonlight bends. Any archer who tells you otherwise has never shot at midnight.
A fighter. Do not chase an archer. Make it come to you. Shield raised, your eyes on its knees, and wait.
A mage. Aim for the archers first. They have no armour against a spell and they have no time to dodge it. The Spellblades are another matter.
A scout. You carry a bow. Show me. No, not that way. Let your elbow float. There. That is a shot.
A healer. A good arrow can drop you from fifty paces. Keep your party within reach of a hand, and your own head below a shield.
Spellblades turn magic aside like rain on a roof. Steel breaks them. They are the one elf that cannot be reasoned with, and the only elf that can be hit.
Wardens are the opposite. Heavy, slow, steady. They hold the line, and they are very, very hard to dent. Lightning cracks them. So does patience.
Aelith was my best student. She could split a leaf at a hundred paces. She never once boasted. I never once told her how proud I was.
Sylas is eager. Eager is a good start and a terrible finish. I am trying to teach him the difference.
Nimue treats the arrow wounds. I treat the arrow-makers. It is a good division of labour.
Selwyn has my only copy of The Archer's Rule. He says it is lost. I say he has misplaced it. We are both right.
A strange trader once offered me an arrow that never missed. I declined. A shot that cannot miss is a shot that cannot be earned.
I used to sing while I shot. It helped the rhythm. I have not sung in three months. My aim has suffered, and so has everything else.
The keep has three galleries. Archers on the first, Spellblades on the second, Wardens on the third. Take them in that order and you will not regret it.
Aelith's lantern is broken, they say. I had a sudden urge to hum. I did. It came out wrong, and it was perfect.
The Hush is over, and my students are cheering. I have told them to keep it down. They have ignored me. Nobody has ever been so glad to be ignored.
You have The Archer's Rule? It is a very short book. It says only: breathe, aim, release, and forgive yourself. The last one has always defeated me.
A thing in the Ruined Stacks half elf, half wraith. I knew it, once. She was a bowmaster of the old school. I had hoped she had found peace.
Shoot well. Shoot calmly. And remember: every arrow is only a question. Some answers are better left unasked.

nimue_fen.name: Nimue Fen
nimue_fen.voice: herb-lore, pulse counts, a healer's trick of asking small questions that unlock large ones

lines.text: A healer's first lesson: listen to the patient before you listen to the pulse. The pulse lies less, but it also says less.
Most of my patients have nothing wrong with them. They are only tired of being quiet. I give them tea and a blanket and ten minutes of not being asked to do anything.
The moon-pool in the south clearing heals fever, bruise and sadness. In that order, and at a steady rate. It is the best doctor in Silverhush.
Moon petals steep into the best remedy for sleeplessness I know. They taste of cold and quiet. Nobody who drinks them wakes up cross.
Clear tea cures the Hush's more stubborn effects: sleep, charm, a lingering curse. I keep a cask by the door. It is the most used thing in my clinic.
I carry a small silver disc under my cloak. The order of Silver Hands has carried one for a thousand years. They say it was the first coin the sun ever spent.
A fighter. Do not take a Warden's hit on the shield arm. It will go numb for an hour. Take it on the plate, and thank your armourer.
A mage. Elven mages cast quickly, and elven bolts bite harder than they seem. Keep your robes dry, and your wits drier.
A scout. If you are taken by one of Taryn's arrows, do not pull it out. Come to me. I will not charge you, I will only scold you.
A healer! I could use a second pair of hands. The sick ward is down the lane. It would mean a great deal, and it would not mean very much to you.
The Hush is a disease of the voice. I know of nothing like it. It took the song out of the body and left a very good imitation of calm.
Captain Aelith had a daughter who sang at her wedding. The Hush took the songs and left the wedding. I think about that more than I should.
Brannoch's tea is my favourite medicine. He does not know. He would stop making it out of embarrassment.
Perrin plays for my patients. Very softly, under a blanket. The fever drops. I have stopped questioning why.
Sylas brought me a hurt owl last week. It was a very good owl. It is much better now, and it has opinions.
Elowen weaves me blankets in the colour of a healthy cheek. I give them to the patients who most need a good complexion.
A trader of strange things gave me a vial that smelled of snow in summer. I used it once. A patient slept for three days, and woke up laughing.
When the Hush ends, plenty of people will have forgotten how to speak. I intend to teach them, one word at a time, over tea.
The Moonwatch Keep is cold, and the Captain's lantern is colder. If you are chilled when you return, come straight to me. I will not scold. Not at once.
Aelith is awake! They brought her to me an hour ago. She asked for a glass of water and then, after months of silence, she began to talk.
With the Hush lifted, my clinic is full of people laughing. Do you know how hard it is to take a pulse when the patient is giggling?
Selwyn's books have come home, and he looks ten years younger. I prescribed more books. He did not argue.
The wraith in the Stacks was one of ours, once. A Silver Hand who stayed to nurse the dying. She stayed too long. I would not go near her, but I would not harm her either.
Whatever you do next, rest when you can. A body is a very good friend, and a very poor liar.

perrin_lark.name: Perrin Lark
perrin_lark.personality: warm, stubborn, irrepressible; the only loud person in town
perrin_lark.voice: rhymes he cannot suppress, chorus lines, and a performer's habit of pausing for applause

lines.text: I walked three hundred miles to sing for the elves, and they have asked me, very politely, to stop. Nothing has ever insulted me so politely as their good manners.
A song is a rumour with a tune. It travels faster than a horse and lasts longer than a king.
I know eleven hundred ballads, forty-one drinking songs and one lullaby. The lullaby is the only one I have ever cried at.
I have been tuning my lute under a blanket for three weeks. It sounds like a very small, very hopeful mouse.
The elves used to sing at dusk, and the whole forest would answer. I heard it once, years ago, from a hill. I have chased it ever since.
A bard's worth is the silence between his notes. The elves are very good at the silence. It is the notes they have forgotten.
A fighter. Expect a verse in your honour: a shield, a blade, a heart unafraid. It rhymes, and it is also true.
Spell-slinger, then. The old star-songs: I know one verse. I know the first verse. It ends in a note no human voice can hold. I have been trying for years.
A scout. I wrote a ballad about a runner once. It was a very fast ballad. Nobody could keep up with the refrain.
A healer. Do you sing, by any chance? A good voice is half a cure, and I have it on the very best authority.
The Hush is a terrible thing, but it has given me one wonderful gift: an audience that is utterly desperate to hear a tune.
Brannoch gives me the corner room. I tune very softly. He pretends not to hear. It is the gentlest favour I have had in a year.
Sylas asked me to teach him a drinking song. I taught him two. He sang them on the bridge at midnight. The Wardens looked the other way.
Nimue claims singing aids the lungs. I claim it aids everything. We are both right, and we have both been fined.
Taryn pretends she does not like my music. I have seen her tapping her foot against the practice-post. It is the best review I have ever received.
A strange peddler once paid for my supper in a single perfect note. It rang for a full minute and then hung in the air. I have never heard anything like it since.
Selwyn has catalogued my entire repertoire. All eleven hundred ballads. I am a footnote in his index and I could not be prouder.
When the Hush lifts, I shall sing from the top of the highest bridge. It will be loud, and it will be flat, and it will be the greatest performance of my life.
The Captain has a lantern that eats songs. I have heard it from across the river, a kind of absence, like a note being swallowed. Break it, if you can.
The lantern is broken! I heard a note come back, across the river. A single, perfect, wavering note. I think it was a thrush.
They sang tonight. The whole town. I stood on the lower bridge with my lute and wept so hard I could not play. It was the best concert I have ever given.
I wrote a verse about the Library's lost tomes. It has four lines and one very sad rhyme. Selwyn has asked to put it in the catalogue.
A ballad about a wraith who sings in the ruins. I have it half written. I should like to hear the original, if the original were not dangerous.
I will write your ballad one day. I will call it The Lamp-Bearer. It will have eleven verses and a chorus everyone can sing. Eventually.

sylas_thorn.name: Sylas Thorn
sylas_thorn.role: young scout of the high bridges
sylas_thorn.voice: breathless descriptions of heights and a stubborn urge to apologise for existing loudly

lines.text: I am Sylas. I am a hundred and four. That is young, for an elf. People say it is very young. I am trying to be older, but it keeps not working.
There are three hundred bridges in Silverhush. I have crossed every one of them. Some of them twice. Backwards, once, on a dare.
The highest bridge is the Moon-Lintel. From the middle you can see the edge of the forest and, on a clear night, the glow of the Rootmere shrine.
I wanted to be an archer. I am not good enough. I wanted to be a healer. I am too clumsy. I settled for scout, and I find I do not mind.
I was out on the forest road when the Hush came down. I saw the lamps go on, one by one, all along the gates. It was beautiful. Then I understood.
I do not like the Hush. I have said so. Twice. Aloud. Taryn said I was very brave. I said I was very afraid. She said that was the same thing.
A fighter! Would you teach me to swing a sword? Not seriously. Just to see how it feels. I promise to put it down when someone shouts.
A mage! Could you conjure a light, a small one? I want to see what it looks like when something glows because someone told it to.
A scout! Have you seen the north bridges? They are very high and very cold and I am secretly terrified of them. Please tell no one.
Healer, may I ask something? What do you do when someone is sad, and there is no herb for it? I have been wondering for weeks.
The elves in the keep are not themselves. Their eyes are flat and their hands are steady. I used to know some of them. I used to share their lunches.
Taryn trained me. She is very strict and very kind. She never says she is proud, but she once straightened my cloak, and It has stayed with me every day since.
Nimue treated my sprained ankle. She gave me a lecture. It was the best lecture I ever received. I wish she had gone on longer.
Perrin taught me a drinking song. It has a very rude chorus. I sing it softly on the bridges, and nobody minds. The trees seem to like it.
Elowen mends my sleeves. I tear them again. It is a game, I suspect, and she is winning.
Some peddler pressed a silver feather on me once. It never lands. I keep it in my pocket and it flutters against my leg, very softly, like a pulse.
Brannoch gives me the stable when the bridges ice over. The cat sleeps on my chest. It is the best bed in Silverhush.
I want to see the sea. I have read about it in Selwyn's books. It is large and loud and has no bridges. I expect I would love it.
The keep is a day east along the road. If you want, Let me guide you over the shortcut. It goes over a very high bridge. I will walk in front. I will not look down.
The captain is free! I saw her walk across the Moon-Lintel and she was laughing! I have never seen an elf run so fast. I ran after her. I fell off. She caught me.
The whole town is loud! Louder than I ever imagined! I am going to shout from the highest bridge, and I do not care who hears!
I found a book on the forest road, wet and torn. It said something about the Hush on page seventeen. Selwyn will want it. I could not bring myself to open it.
There is a ghost in the Ruined Stacks. I saw her once, from the road. She was singing. I ran so fast my shadow got lost.
Should you need a guide through the Frostwake, I know every branch. Well, most of them. A few of them. At least the ones that hold.
